original_card.question: Does one quantified step of the proposed #4100 all-size construction hold at its actual caller?
methods: Prove one missing implication with explicit quantified hypotheses.
Find an exact counterexample at the claimed interface boundary.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Identify the proposition and what would change downstream; do not equate a finite replay with a universal proof.

first_step.inspect: Read PROOF.md and AUDIT.md in #4100. Select one distinct obligation: CRT total repair, native/free-algebra lifting, precision/conditioning, or complete fixed-tape cost. This is an author-submitted proof, not an accepted unconditional theorem.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; no scientific replay, theorem acceptance or supplier admission. Budget any heavy replay separately.

original_card.first_experiment: Check live handoffs; name one proposition, its caller, quantified domain and dependency closure. Independently prove the implication or exhibit a precise gap/counterexample. Prioritize CRT.md total repair or COMPLEX.md free-algebra lift only if unclaimed. Stop at the chosen obligation; do not substitute finite samples or root arithmetic for an all-size proof, or launch the complete package by default.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Finite supplier improvements are useful only under the retained transfer obligations.
allowed_variations: One CRT repair, native lift, precision/conditioning or tape-cost proposition, with its exact caller.
scope_change_triggers: Replacing a quantified obligation with another finite smoke test.
Treating archive intake, an author PASS receipt or a finite composed fixture as discharge of the universal hypotheses.

existing_checks.scope: PR #4100: proposed unconditional construction and finite checks, without independent acceptance.
existing_checks.remaining: Independent proof audit of one caller-bound all-size implication; all other premises remain explicit.

actual_scope: Decide the disjoint-guard premise of #4100 CRT.md section 4 under position-mod-K coloring: a window lemma, a counterexample to the literal K-bit guard on #4100's own gadget, and a census of #4174's actual production placement descriptors, plus eight further admitted width patterns and two adversarial ones.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for one quantified implication at its caller; this is the guard hypothesis that #4321 and #4328 assume and no audit decided, checked at the actual caller's descriptors (#4174).
bottleneck_link: The compact switch's correctness and the bad-density term both rest on this premise; a wrong window convention breaks the gadget on good addresses.
stop_rule: Stop once the premise is decided (lemma plus counterexample) and checked on #4174's production descriptors.
evidence: verify.py: 3,266 exhaustive lemma cases; #4100's gadget on all 2^20 two-target addresses at spacing K: (K-1)-bit guards give S=T on all 82,944 good addresses, K-bit guards fail on 3,888/2,388 good addresses and T leaves the good set on 31,104/15,552; #4174 production census (104,864 plans, 524,288 axis visits): all axes in y, zero possible same-color pairs for any Benes schedule, aligned multiplicity 1, 16,225 plans with last-K exception axes; eight more admitted patterns (blocked both ways, uniform 24, uniform 23, three random, ell=32): zero possible same-color pairs; uniform 24 misses a multiple of K by one bit, and the admitted pattern with ell-1 axes 16384..16407 puts aligned same-color targets exactly K apart at 24 layers, where (K-1)-bit windows are checked target-free.
author: Ryanson Jonathan, with Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5) assistance
ai_assistance: Substantial Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5) assistance in reading, the lemma, census implementation and writing; no independent human or proof-kernel review.

open_questions.question: Price compact macros per occupied color rather than per residue mod K.

open_questions.first_step: Bound occupied colors per batch by r_max in the CRT section 4 cost line.

open_questions.why_it_matters: An admitted layout puts same-color targets exactly K apart, so the literal K-bit guard fails there; #4321's hypothesis wording follows the text.
open_questions.first_step: Restate the predicate with (K-1)-bit windows and re-derive the 8B/2^K term.
